clue.text: Band's journey through the Home Counties

indicators.note: the journey runs through the region, so one piece sits inside the other

parts.note: the Home Counties are the counties around London, in the SE (south-east) of England
a trip is a journey

explanation.surface: A band's tour route taking it through the commuter counties around London.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Band's' reads as the band's possession, but the 's is just 'is' linking definition to wordplay. The Home Counties surround London in south-east England, abbreviated SE.
explanation.definitionFit: A stripe is a narrow band of colour, as on a flag or shirt.

clue.text: Party-goer, i.e. A-list company, possibly

indicators.note: possibly signals that the letters could be arranged in some other order

explanation.surface: A party-goer seen as one of the A-list crowd, presumably.
explanation.walkthrough: 'possibly' rearranges IE, ALIST and CO together.
explanation.definitionFit: A socialite is someone well known in fashionable society, a regular at parties and glamorous events.

clue.text: Story's an introduction to Caesar in his city

indicators.note: in says the short pieces sit inside the city's name

parts.note: Caesar's city is Rome

indicators.note: the introduction to a word is its opening letter

explanation.surface: A tale that begins with Julius Caesar arriving in Rome.
explanation.walkthrough: AN plus C (the start of Caesar) goes inside ROME, the city of Caesar.
explanation.definitionFit: A romance is a story of love or adventure, a common sense in literature.

clue.text: Stop apricots being stewed for snack food

indicators.note: stewing fruit breaks it down and mixes it, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: An instruction to stop stewing apricots and eat something else instead.
explanation.walkthrough: 'being stewed' rearranges STOP and APRICOTS together; 'Stop' looks like a command but is fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Crisps made from thin fried slices of potato are a classic packet snack.

clue.text: Sailors taking on the world appear wholly engaging

definitions.note: a participle phrase, standing for the verb sense engage wholly

indicators.note: taking on means the sailors acquire the next piece, which follows them

parts.note: ABs are able seamen, so ABS stands for sailors
an orb is a sphere, here the globe or world

explanation.surface: Sailors who take on the whole world seem totally gripping.
explanation.walkthrough: ABS (able seamen) followed by ORB; 'appear' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: To absorb someone is to occupy their attention completely, to engross them.

clue.text: Mention item of jewellery found in turning over bar

indicators.note: found in says the jewellery sits inside the other piece
turning over says the word for a bar is read backwards in this down clue

parts.note: a pub is a bar
a ring is an item of jewellery

explanation.surface: Someone mentions a ring discovered while a pub was being searched.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turning over' makes BUP from PUB, and 'found in' puts RING inside, giving B-RING-UP.
explanation.definitionFit: To bring up a subject is to raise or mention it in conversation.

clue.text: Theatrical production in square posters sent up

indicators.note: sent up says the hidden letters are read backwards
the clue word that says the letters sit inside the next words

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A stage show advertised on posters in a town square, though mocked.
explanation.walkthrough: The run AREPO spans 'squARE POsters'; 'sent up' turns it upward in this down clue. 'sent up' looks like mockery but is the reversal signal.
explanation.definitionFit: An opera is a staged drama set to music, a kind of theatrical work.

clue.text: 60s rebel to get better of upset family

indicators.note: to here joins the second piece on after the first

parts.note: to beat someone is to get the better of them

indicators.note: upset in a down clue means turned upside down, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: kin means family

explanation.surface: A young rebel of the sixties beats an upset family in an argument.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' turns KIN into NIK after BEAT.
explanation.definitionFit: A beatnik was a member of the Beat Generation, the bohemian youth counterculture of the late 1950s and 1960s.

clue.text: One not entirely lifeless concept

parts.note: the Roman numeral I is one

indicators.note: not entirely means the word is used without its final letter

parts.note: dead means lifeless

explanation.surface: A thought that is only partly dead.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not entirely' trims DEAD to DEA, after I for one.
explanation.definitionFit: A concept is a notion or thought, a plain synonym.

clue.text: Inflict great damage on returning vermin in time

indicators.note: in says the backward vermin sits inside the time

parts.note: a date is a point in time

indicators.note: returning says the word for vermin is read backwards

parts.note: mice are vermin

explanation.surface: Vermin coming back in season and wreaking havoc.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returning' turns MICE into ECIM, which goes inside DATE.
explanation.definitionFit: To decimate originally meant killing one in ten, now loosely to destroy a large part of something.

clue.text: Films blokes kept back in custody of spies

indicators.note: in custody of says the blokes are held inside the spies

parts.note: the CIA is the American spy agency

indicators.note: kept back says the word for blokes is turned round

parts.note: men are blokes

explanation.surface: Some men are being held by intelligence agents.
explanation.walkthrough: 'kept back' turns MEN into NEM, held inside CIA.
explanation.definitionFit: Cinema means films collectively, the art or industry of motion pictures.

clue.text: Encouraging eating mushy peas? That's mean

indicators.note: eating says one piece takes the other inside it

parts.note: cheering means encouraging

indicators.note: mushy peas are mashed, so the letters are mashed into a new order

explanation.surface: A remark that it is mean to cheer someone on while they eat mushy peas.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mushy' rearranges PEAS to SEPA, which goes inside CHEERING. Mushy peas are a British side dish of mashed marrowfat peas; 'That's' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Cheeseparing describes stingy, miserly penny-pinching, so it is an adjective for being mean.

clue.text: Not favouring whisky, unlike everyone else?

explanation.surface: Someone who shuns whisky, out of step with everyone else.
explanation.walkthrough: The first reading splits the phrase as AGAINST (not favouring) plus THE GRAIN, grain whisky.
explanation.definitionFit: Against the grain means contrary to the usual or natural direction; read literally, it is opposing grain spirit, a kind of whisky.

clue.text: Supposed expert showing main source of current in flex

indicators.note: in says the pieces sit inside the flex

parts.note: flex is British for an electric cable or wire
the main is a literary name for the sea

indicators.note: the source of a word is its opening letter

explanation.surface: An expert showing where the electricity comes into a cable.
explanation.walkthrough: SEA plus C (the start of current) goes inside WIRE. 'main' looks electrical, as in mains supply, but means the sea.
explanation.definitionFit: A wiseacre is a know-all, someone who claims more knowledge than they have.

clue.text: Courage and power leading to good fortune

indicators.note: leading to puts the first piece in front of the second

parts.note: P is the physics symbol for power
luck is good fortune

explanation.surface: Courage and strength bring good fortune.
explanation.definitionFit: Pluck is spirited bravery, a synonym for courage.

clue.text: One whose field of expertise hasn't been identified

definitions.text: One whose field of expertise hasn't been identified

parts.words: One whose field of expertise hasn't been identified
parts.note: reads like a specialist with no known subject, but it is someone who studies unidentified flying objects

explanation.walkthrough: The specialism is objects that are by definition unidentified.
explanation.definitionFit: This specialist studies reports of unidentified flying objects.

clue.text: Satisfies hunting groups

definitions.meaning: a plural noun: gatherings of fox-hunters

explanation.definitionFit: To satisfy a need is to fulfil it; also, gatherings of riders and hounds for a hunt share the same name.

clue.text: Spooky horse seen around hansom

indicators.note: around says the horse surrounds the carriage

parts.note: a mare is a female horse
a hansom is a horse-drawn cab

explanation.surface: An eerie horse seen pulling a Victorian carriage.
explanation.walkthrough: A hansom is a two-wheeled horse-drawn cab of Victorian London.
explanation.definitionFit: Macabre means gruesome or ghastly, dealing with death, so spooky.

clue.text: Left to tuck into hot sweet fruitcake

indicators.note: to tuck into says one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: hot is slang for stolen goods

explanation.surface: Leftover fruitcake to be eaten while still warm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tuck into' suggests eating, but puts L inside STOLEN.
explanation.definitionFit: Stollen is a German fruit bread eaten at Christmas.

clue.text: Cope with rain in storm? It should protect against colder weather

annotationWithheld.why: Clue as held 'Cope with rain in storm? It should protect against colder weather (3-5)' is for a hyphenated 3-5 answer about protection from cold; it does not fit IDEATION, and no search found the matching clue
annotationWithheld.clue: Cope with rain in storm? It should protect against colder weather

clue.text: In that place is a saint

parts.note: there means in that place
S is a short form of is, as in it's

explanation.surface: A saint is to be found in that spot.
explanation.definitionFit: St Theresa (Teresa of Ávila) is a Spanish saint and mystic.

clue.text: Writing for oneself, not novel as literary work?

parts.note: commonplace means ordinary, the opposite of novel
a book is a literary work

explanation.surface: A private journal, not a novel, offered as a piece of literature.
explanation.walkthrough: 'novel' looks like a type of book but means new; 'as' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A commonplace book is a personal notebook of quotations and jottings kept for its owner's use.

clue.text: Mother — and her relationship with father?

definitions.meaning: Latin and old public-school slang for one's mum
she is father's mate, so read as one who mates

explanation.definitionFit: Mater is Latin for mother; as a made-up agent noun from mate it describes a wife's role as partner.

clue.text: English county known to Scots

definitions.meaning: Scots ken means know, with past form meaning known

explanation.definitionFit: Kent is the county in England's south-east corner; in Scots, kent is the past participle of ken, to know.

clue.text: Nebuchadnezzar's courage

definitions.meaning: a huge wine container holding twenty standard measures

explanation.definitionFit: A Nebuchadnezzar is an oversized wine vessel; in British slang having the nerve to do something is having the bottle.

clue.text: One kind of European, or second kind of European

parts.note: an Iberian is a native of Spain or Portugal

explanation.surface: A riddle comparing two sorts of European.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is loose: Siberia lies in Russia, a European nation, though geographically in Asia.
explanation.definitionFit: A Siberian is a native of Siberia, part of Russia, so a type of Russian.

clue.text: Queen's tirade not following usual custom?

parts.note: ER (Elizabeth Regina) is the Queen; the 's is a link
a rant is a tirade

explanation.surface: The Queen breaks with protocol to deliver an angry rant.
explanation.walkthrough: ER stands for Elizabeth Regina, Queen Elizabeth.
explanation.definitionFit: Errant means straying from the proper course or accepted standards.

clue.text: Shocked as snow's beginning in a mountain pass

indicators.note: in places the letter inside the other pieces

parts.note: a ghat is a mountain pass in India

indicators.note: the beginning of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: Travellers horrified as snow starts falling in a mountain pass.
explanation.walkthrough: S (the start of snow) goes inside A GHAT; ghat is an Indian word for a pass. 'as' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Aghast means filled with horror or amazement.
